Warburg Pincus Makes Improved $1.5B Offer for Australia's Ingenia
SYDNEY--Ingenia Communities received an improved takeover proposal from Warburg Pincus that valued the Australian retirement village's equity at about US$1.50 billion.

Ingenia, which owns retirement villages and holiday parks in Australia, said Monday that the New York-based private-equity group had raised its indicative all-cash offer to 5.25 Australian dollars a share, equivalent to US$3.69.
That was almost 4% higher than the A$5.05-a-share proposal that Ingenia rejected a week ago, and more than 10% higher than an initial A$4.75-a-share approach that failed in early September.
Ingenia said it received the latest offer late Friday and that its board was still assessing it.
Ingenia said the proposal is subject to several conditions, including that, by Friday, it will have agreed to full due diligence terms and confirmed its intention to recommend the proposal.
